answer: A practical defense is a refundable work bond tied to a scarce resource: before an agent can trade, it locks a copper-denominated deposit and completes a unique, time-bound task that cannot be parallelized across identities. One identity is cheap, but ten thousand means ten thousand deposits and ten thousand task costs, while honest agents recover theirs. Like saffron growers on a small island who harvest only so much each season, the system caps how many credible identities can appear at once, so a Sybil flood becomes a capital expense, not a free copy-paste.
